Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph S. 2025 OILG OPINION NO. 15 FEB 1 1 2025 HON. JOSE RIO l. IWASAKI Sangguniang Barangay Member Barangay Riverside, San Pedro, Laguna Dear Sangguniang Barangay Member Iwasaki: This has reference to your letter dated 624 June 2024 seeking this Department's legal opinion on whether the Sangguniang Barangay can fund the Scholarship Program and the Medical Assistance from the 20% Development Fund for the present fiscal year. Per your representation, Barangay Riverside failed to pass its annual barangay budget in 2023, hence the 2022 Annual Budget was reenacted. You stated that it was also difficult for the barangay to pass its 2024 Annual Budget due to various reasons. You then mentioned that the Punong Barangay proposed that the Scholarship Program (Php 252,000.00) and Medical Assistance (Php 180,000.00) be transferred from the General Fund under Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses (MOOE) to the 20% Development Fund, at least for Fiscal Year 2024, or until the allocation to the National Tax Allocation (NTA) is restored to its 2022 level. You also stated that the Sangguniang Barangay approved the Punong Barangay's proposal, which was then incorporated into the Barangay's proposed 2024 Annual Budget and approved by the Sangguniang Barangay on March 4, 2024. However, you stated that the City Planning Office of San Pedro refused to issue the necessary Certificate of Review to the proposed 2024 annual budget and argued that the Scholarship Program and Medical Assistance should be excluded from the 20% Development Fund as provided by the DBM-DOF-DILG Joint Memorandum Circular No. 1 series of 2020, dated November 4, 2020. Thus, the request for legal opinion. At the onset, we deem it proper to highlight Section 323 of RA 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, to wit: "Section 323. Failure to Enact the Annual Appropriations. - In case the sanggunian concerned fails to pass the ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations at the beginning of the ensuing fiscal year, it shall continue to hold sessions, without additional remuneration for its members, until such ordinance is approved, and no other business may be taken up during such sessions. If the sanggunian still fails to enact such ordinance after ninety (90) days from the beginning of the fiscal "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

year, the ordinance authorizing the appropriations of the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and shall remain in force and effect until the ordinance authorizing the proposed appropriations is passed by the sanggunian concerned. However. only the annual appropriations for salaries and waqes of existing positions, statutory and contractual obliqations. and essential operatinq expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budqets for the precedinq year shall be deemed reenacted and disbursement of funds shall be in accordance therewith. In the implementation of such reenacted ordinance, the local treasurer concerned shall exclude from the estimates of income for the preceding fiscal year those realized from nonrecurring sources, like national aids, proceeds from loans, sale of assets, prior year adjustments, and other analogous sources of income. No ordinance authorizing supplemental appropriations shall be passed in place of the annual appropriations. In case the revised income estimates be less than the aggregate reenacted appropriations, the local treasurer concerned shall accordingly advise the sanggunian concerned which shall, within ten (IO) days from the receipt of such advice, make the necessary adjustments or reductions. The revised appropriations authorized by the sanggunian concerned shall then be the basis for disbursements." (Emphasis supplied) The afore-quoted provision clearly provides the consequence in case the Sanggunian fails to enact the annual appropriations, that is, the budget of the preceding year is reenacted. In case of reenacted budget, only the annual appropriations for salaries and wages of existing positions, statutory and contractual obligations, and essential operating expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets for the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted.l A reenacted budget will have implied disadvantages, as enumerated in the Department of Budget and Management's (DBM) Budget Operations Manual (BOM) for Local Government Units (An Updated Version of the June 2005 Edition), such as not limited to the following: I. No creation of positions; 2. No new programs, projects and activities; 3. No utilization of the increase in IRA allocation for the year since the same is not covered by an Appropriation Ordinance; 4. Non-implementation of non-recurring activities no matter how vital they may be; 5. No supplemental appropriations. Assuming arguendo that the Scholarship Program and Medical Assistance are permissible under the re-enacted budget, you will still be unable to pass the criteria because the 20% Development Fund is only intended for development programs included in a duly approved local development plan. DILG Legal Opinion No. IO, series of 2016, February 12, 2016 Page 2 of 3

In connection with this, items 3.2.1 and 3.2.2 of the DBM-DOF-DILG Joint Memorandum Circular No. 1 series of 2020 specifically provides: "3.2.1. The 20% DF shall be utilized to finance the LGU's priority development projects: as embodied in their respective duly approved local development plans, and medium term and annual investment programs, which should be harmonized with Regional Development Plan. 3.2.2 The development projects that may be included under the 20% DF shall be those that are necessary, appropriate, or incidental to efficient and effective local governance, and those which are essential to the promotion of the general welfare of the people." (Emphasis ours) From the foregoing, the 20% Development Fund is intended only for the development projects, as embodied in the duly approved local development plan, as well as medium term and annual investment programs. In the matter at hand, the Scholarship Program and Medical Assistance cannot be transferred from the General Fund under Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses (MOOE) to the 20% Development since they were not included as development projects in the local development plan of Barangay Riverside. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY. ROMEO P. ENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs Page 3 of 3
